native_result.query: In the PCA conducted on forms of capital, analyzed in hundred-year time slices, how are the symbolic capital components such as house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords characterized in terms of their values on the first principal component (PC1) and distribution across the second principal component (PC2)?
native_result.HypoA: Symbolic capital components such as house size, the number of daggers, and hatchets/swords are characterized by negative values on the first principal component (PC1) and exhibit a wide distribution of values on the second principal component (PC2). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In the PCA of twelve forms of capital across the 39 hundred-year time slices (4300–500 BCE), house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords all load positively on PC1 (hatchets/swords +0.30, daggers +0.27, house size +0.23), meaning they covary together with the dominant axis of capital accumulation, though none is the strongest PC1 driver (ranks 5/6/10 of 12). Their distinguishing feature is their distribution across PC2: daggers (+0.07) and hatchets/swords (+0.05) hug the PC1 axis with near-zero PC2 loadings (ranked 10th and 12th), whereas house size loads strongly and positively on PC2 (+0.33, rank 5th, correlation 0.50), so in the PC1–PC2 plane house size is rotated ~40–46° away from daggers and hatchets/swords. House size is therefore the symbolic capital component that spreads along PC2, while daggers and hatchets/swords are essentially PC1-only components.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Parsed capital.csv (comma-decimal CSV) into a 39×12 Z-matrix (39 century slices × 12 capital forms). 2) Standardized each variable and ran SVD-based PCA on the pooled slices (correlation-based); fixed the arbitrary PC sign by making the largest-|loading| variable positive per PC. 3) Extracted PC1/PC2 loadings, correlation loadings, explained variance, and per-century PC1/PC2 scores; computed loading-vector angles from the PC1 axis and the PC2 score distribution/group means. 4) Characterized ZAxtSchwert, ZDolch, Zhausgr via PC1 sign/magnitude/rank and PC2 placement/spread. 5) Consistency: confirmed capital.csv's 37 overlapping rows equal time_series raw values exactly (max abs diff 0.0 over 444 cells) and that a 37-row PCA on either source gives identical loadings; reported the 39-vs-37 sensitivity. 6) Pollen openness data excluded (environment context, not a capital form). Executed scripts: analysis_pca_capital.py (main analysis), supplementary.py (angular spread + artifact export).
